overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via a member's email to a quorum, but found no deliberation in the health agent's email with the draft notice; ordered compliance and member training.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting; a member's June 2023 email with edits sent to a quorum was the deliberation at issue.
allegations.key_passage: We find, and the Board admits, that the email shared by Ms. Catalano contained improper deliberation because the email reached a quorum of the Board and included the member’s opinion on a matter within the Board’s jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Complaint's email claim also covered a health agent's email sending all members a draft notice with an attached document drafted by the chair.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the document did not contain any of Chair Hoffman’s own opinions but rather summarized and shared factual information about the requirements of the regulation as well as Title 5 of the State Environmental Code.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements
All Board members attend an Attorney General-conducted Open Meeting Law webinar training within 60 days
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
